comparisons.peer_summary: AMD faces potential intellectual property infringement claims from third parties that could result in substantial damages, injunctions stopping product sales, or costly licensing and redesign efforts, any of which could have a material adverse effect on the business.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose risks related to third-party intellectual property infringement claims that could impact their business. MU highlights potential liabilities arising from its indemnification obligations to defend customers against such IP claims, noting these may include patents, trademarks, copyrights, or trade secrets. Similarly, AMD describes being notified of or having actions brought against it and its customers for alleged IP infringement, with potential consequences including substantial damages, injunctions stopping product sales, or costly licensing efforts.

sentences.text: Such claims, investigations, inquiries, and proceedings may include, but are not limited to, allegations of anticompetitive conduct and infringement of intellectual property.

• our indemnification obligations, including obligations to defend our customers against third-party claims asserting infringement of certain intellectual property rights, which may include patents, trademarks, copyrights, or trade secrets; and

With respect to intellectual property litigation, from time to time, we have been notified of, or third parties may bring or have brought, actions against us and/or against our customers based on allegations that we are infringing the intellectual property rights of others, contributing to or inducing the infringement of the intellectual property rights of others, improperly claiming ownership of intellectual property or otherwise improperly using the intellectual property of others.

These parties may file lawsuits against us or our customers seeking damages (potentially up to and including treble damages) or an injunction against the sale of products that incorporate allegedly infringed intellectual property or against the operation of our business as presently conducted, which could result in our having to stop the sale of some of our products or to increase the costs of selling some of our products or which could damage our reputation.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD is a party to various legal actions, including securities, corporate governance, consumer class actions, product liability, and environmental claims from former manufacturing facilities. Outcomes are uncertain, and successful claims could result in material damages, substantial costs, or prohibitions on selling products.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose exposure to product liability and warranty claims as part of their broader litigation risks. MU explicitly lists 'the terms of our product warranties or from product liability claims' as a source of litigation. AMD similarly notes that its products, being purchased by and used by consumers, increase its exposure to 'consumer actions such as product liability claims and consumer class action claims.' While both mention these claims, AMD places them within a broader context of securities and corporate governance litigation, whereas MU links them directly to product performance and warranty terms.

sentences.text: • the terms of our product warranties or from product liability claims.
Our products are purchased by and/or used by consumers, which could increase our exposure to consumer actions such as product liability claims and consumer class action claims.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces warranty claims, product recalls, and product liability, with potential liabilities that may be significant, unlimited, and exceed revenue from relevant products. Reserves and insurance may be inadequate to cover uninsured portions of such claims, materially affecting financial condition.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO disclose significant risks related to product warranties and product liability. MU identifies liabilities arising from 'the terms of our product warranties or from product liability claims' as a specific source of legal disputes. AVGO provides more detail, stating it is subject to 'warranty claims, product recalls and product liability' and that potential liabilities can be 'significant, and in some cases... potentially unlimited,' potentially exceeding revenue from relevant products. Both companies acknowledge these as material sources of financial exposure.

sentences.text: • the terms of our product warranties or from product liability claims.
We are subject to warranty claims, product recalls and product liability.
The potential liabilities associated with such provisions are significant, and in some cases, including in agreements with some of our largest customers, are potentially unlimited.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intellectual Property Litigation Risks and Consequences
comparisons.peer_summary: Third parties, including non-practicing entities, assert IP claims against Intel, which can increase costs, disrupt operations, and harm reputation. Specific examples include an injunction obtained by R2 Semiconductor in Germany in February 2024 and adverse judgments in VLSI and R2 cases. IP claims may require Intel to pay damages, indemnify customers, stop manufacturing products, or enter costly license agreements, potentially harming its competitive position and requiring asset impairments.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC face risks from third-party intellectual property infringement claims. MU states it is subject to 'allegations of ... infringement of intellectual property' and must defend customers against third-party IP claims. INTC similarly faces 'claims based on IP rights against us and our products' from various entities, which can cause large costs to respond to and defend, diverting management attention. Both companies highlight that these IP disputes can result in significant financial and operational burdens.

sentences.text: Such claims, investigations, inquiries, and proceedings may include, but are not limited to, allegations of anticompetitive conduct and infringement of intellectual property.

• our indemnification obligations, including obligations to defend our customers against third-party claims asserting infringement of certain intellectual property rights, which may include patents, trademarks, copyrights, or trade secrets; and
Third parties assert claims based on IP rights against us and our products, which could harm our business.

Claims that our products, technologies, or processes infringe the IP rights of others, regardless of their merits, cause us to incur large costs to respond to, defend, and resolve the claims, and they divert the efforts and attention of our management and technical personnel from our business and operations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intellectual Property Litigation and Protection Costs
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA faces risks from IP infringement lawsuits and the costs associated with protecting its IP rights, including potential damages, injunctions, and license payments, which could harm its competitive position or operating results.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA disclose risks associated with intellectual property litigation and the costs of defending against infringement claims. MU notes it is subject to 'allegations of ... infringement of intellectual property' and faces claims where it must 'defend our customers against third-party claims asserting infringement.' NVDA similarly reports being 'involved in lawsuits or other legal proceedings alleging patent infringement or other IP rights violations' and that such claims 'could cause us to incur significant costs to respond to, defend, and resolve such claims.' Both companies emphasize the financial and operational cost of these IP disputes.

• our indemnification obligations, including obligations to defend our customers against third-party claims asserting infringement of certain intellectual property rights, which may include patents, trademarks, copyrights, or trade secrets; and
From time to time, we are involved in lawsuits or other legal proceedings alleging patent infringement or other IP rights violations by us, our employees or parties that we have agreed to indemnify.

Claims that our products or processes infringe the IP rights of others, regardless of their merit, could cause us to incur significant costs to respond to, defend, and resolve such claims, and they may also divert the efforts and attention of management and technical personnel.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm is subject to various governmental investigations and legal proceedings, with key allegations including violations of FRAND licensing commitments, excessive royalty rates, and antitrust concerns. The company may face additional litigation or investigations in the future.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM disclose risks related to allegations of anticompetitive conduct. MU states that its legal claims may include 'allegations of anticompetitive conduct.' QCOM is subject to governmental investigations and legal proceedings with key allegations including that it 'violate antitrust laws and engage in anticompetitive conduct and unfair methods of competition.' Both companies identify this as a specific source of legal and regulatory scrutiny.

sentences.text: Such claims, investigations, inquiries, and proceedings may include, but are not limited to, allegations of anticompetitive conduct and infringement of intellectual property.

Certain of these matters are described in this Annual Report in "Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 7. Commitments and Contingencies." Key allegations or findings in those matters include or have in the past included, among others: that we violate FRAND licensing commitments by refusing to grant licenses to chipset manufacturers; that our royalty rates are too high; that the base on which our royalties are calculated should be something less than the wholesale (i.e., licensee's) selling price of the applicable device (minus certain permitted deductions); that we unlawfully require customers to execute a patent license before we sell them cellular modem chipsets; that we have entered into exclusive agreements with chipset customers that foreclose competition; that we leverage our position in baseband chipsets in the RFFE space; and that we violate antitrust laws and engage in anticompetitive conduct and unfair methods of competition.
